provider: SURF Research Drive (Netherlands) — up to 5 TB free via NWO-funded Small Compute applications

free_tier.stated: Community Edition: 'Are you working at an institution without its own Research Drive environment? Then apply for access to Research Drive Community Edition here. You will receive up to 5 TB of storage space.' Institutional instances have their own (much larger) quotas set per institution.
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: No per-object cap documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
per_object_cap.notes: extraction found no per-object clause; some of these providers meter on object count rather than bytes, and some state no cap

retention.stated: No retention statement documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
retention.notes: extraction found no retention clause; the seed's limits text may still state one, see extras.limits_verbatim

egress.terms: Unmetered. SURF is the Dutch national e-infrastructure, no egress product exists.

tooling: Research Drive is ownCloud/Nextcloud-based, so the standard desktop sync client and WebDAV endpoints work; rclone's webdav backend applies. Not S3.
chaining: Grants 5 TB per project via Small Compute. The same application also provides up to 10 TB project storage on Snellius, up to 200 TB disk storage and 300 TB tape storage on Grid/Spider for data processing, and up to 50 TB offline tape storage.
limits_note: Per-object-cap: not published for Research Drive; the SURF bundle page caps 'max. 10TB project space storage' on Snellius and 'up to 200TB disk storage' on Grid/Spider. request-rate: not published. Retention: tied to the project; SURF states data is retained for the project duration. Gate: 'researchers must have either a tenured appointment .. or a tenure track appointment at one of the research organisations listed'. A genuinely institution-gated, NWO-funded scheme.

extras.agent_focus: National and regional research-data infrastructure that hands out free (or grant-funded) bulk object storage to researchers: EUDAT/B2SHARE, EOSC EU Node, SURF, GÉANT ecosystem, NIRD/Sigma2, CSC Allas + LUMI-O, NAISS, DeiC, EuroHPC, DARIAH/CLARIN/ELIXIR nodes, NCI, ARDC Nectar, Digital Alliance of Canada, ACCESS/OSN, TACC, NCAR, NRP. Central question: which of these are SELF-SERVICE (anyone can get a login and a bucket) versus INSTITUTION-GATED (you need a university appointment, a national research affiliation, or a reviewed proposal). The per-project quotas here are the largest numbers in the whole survey — 10-150 TB — so the gate, not the quota, is the finding.
